newsitem.title: USA: US extends textile pact with China citing progress.
newsitem.headline: US extends textile pact with China citing progress.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky announced Monday that the 1994 bilateral textile agreement with China would be extended until Jan. 31 next year amid progress in talks on renewing the pact.

The agreement was set to expire on Dec. 31, but Barshefsky said in a statement that a third round of negotiations held in San Francisco earlier this month resulted in an outline of the scope and issues to be covered in a new accord.
"I am pleased that our negotiating team led by Ambassador Rita Hayes is making progess," she said.
Another round of talks was proposed for late January in Beijing.

Barshefsky said the extra 30 days would provide the necessary time to resolve outstanding issues. The eventual pact must deal with illegal transhipments and meet the basic principle of allowing the United States to sell products in China.
The United States slapped penalties of $19 million on Chinese textile imports back in September, saying China was shipping products though third countries to avoid quota restrictions.
Beijing had initially threatened to temporarily halt imports of U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks if the penalties were not withdrawn.
But earlier this Month, China said it would delay those plans in light of further talks on the matter.
